text: The bug was an off-by-one in `sliding_window`: `enumerate(itertools.tee(seq, n), 1)` started indices at 1 instead of 0, so each of the `n` tee'd iterators had one extra element skipped via `itertools.islice(it, i)` before consumption, shifting/dropping the first window (and eliminating any windows when the sequence length equals `n`). Changing the enumeration to start at 0 (the default) makes the i-th iterator skip exactly `i` elements as intended, restoring the correct first window and count of `L - n + 1` windows.

final_text: The bug was an off-by-one in `sliding_window`: `enumerate(itertools.tee(seq, n), 1)` started indices at 1 instead of 0, so each of the `n` tee'd iterators had one extra element skipped via `itertools.islice(it, i)` before consumption, shifting/dropping the first window (and eliminating any windows when the sequence length equals `n`). Changing the enumeration to start at 0 (the default) makes the i-th iterator skip exactly `i` elements as intended, restoring the correct first window and count of `L - n + 1` windows.
